Five ways to give a sparse dashboard weight

Each proposal is shown with one project holding one orb, then with three projects. The variant control in each frame's top bar switches proposals.

1 · Full-height ruled board · one project

Columns run to the bottom of the viewport and their empty remainder is ruled like ledger paper. The page is a surface, not a stub.

1 · Full-height ruled board · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.

2 · Fleet strip and footer · one project

A top strip with live totals and a bottom strip with system facts frame the board. Columns fill the space between.

2 · Fleet strip and footer · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.

3 · Large type · one project

Project names at 26px, orb names at 15px, wider columns, more padding. Substance through scale, nothing added.

3 · Large type · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.

4 · Recent activity ledger · one project

A RECENT section lists the lifecycle edges the system already records, most recent first, filling the empty space with real history.

4 · Recent activity ledger · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.

5 · Slot grid · one project

A fixed grid of slots always fills the width. Projects and New Project occupy slots; the rest are drawn as empty dashed cells.

5 · Slot grid · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.

6 · Fleet strip, footer, and moderate type · one project

Proposal 2's totals strip and system footer with full-height columns, plus project names at 18px and orb names at 14px. Columns 316px so four fit at 1280.

6 · Fleet strip, footer, and moderate type · three projects

Same proposal with more on the board.
